title: Pipkin and Bartholomew's Brave New Chart
markdown:
Right then, adventurers! Gather ‘round! I’ve got a tale from Willowbrook, a village so neat you could eat off the pavement. In Willowbrook lived Pipkin, the dentist’s assistant. Pipkin noticed something important: the children were terrified of Dr. Gnash’s chomping chair.

“This won’t do!” Pipkin declared. He put on his thinking cap and rummaged through his treasure chest for glitter and sharp crayons. That’s how he dreamt up the Willowbrook Bravery Chart. This wasn't just paper; it was a map to courage! Every time a child sat still or managed a tiny, nervous smile, Pipkin awarded a golden star. Soon, the clinic walls were dazzling with sparkly smiles and stickers. Absolutely marvelous!

Deep in the whispering woods lived Kit the badger, Della the terrier, and Professor Pine the owl. Kit loved collecting stars. Della wondered what *truly* made a smile brave. Professor Pine declared it a "fascinating deviation from the norm."

Then, one blustery afternoon, Bartholomew Higgins stomped into Willowbrook. He was a mole whose disposition was as sour as old jam. Bartholomew detested all the cheerful commotion. “Smiling? It’s a sham!” he grumbled, his nose twitching. “Real bravery is quiet. It’s deep down!”

Kit, confused, puffed out his chest and offered Bartholomew his biggest, star-worthy grin. Della noticed Bartholomew’s grumpy expression didn’t budge. Professor Pine politely inquired, “And what might your name be, sir, and your thoughts on this custom?”

“Bartholomew Higgins,” he huffed, like rustling dry leaves. “This village has gone daft about teeth! Bravery is facing the dark, not flaunting enamel!” Kit and Della exchanged glances. Bartholomew was unmoved by their triumphs.

Bartholomew sighed, like wind whistling through a log. His gruffness softened. “Look,” he confessed, his voice barely a whisper, “I’m just… not good at smiling. People stare. So, I decided it was easier to just… not. My bravery is hidden because I hide when it comes to cheerful displays.” He shuffled his feet. “I spend my days digging, facing the dark and the damp. That’s brave, isn’t it? But no one gives you a sticker for it.”

Pipkin, who had joined their huddle, heard Bartholomew’s words. His kind heart did a somersault. “Mr. Higgins,” Pipkin said gently, his smile warm as summer, “you’re absolutely right. Bravery comes in all shapes. Digging deep takes incredible courage. Perhaps,” Pipkin’s eyes twinkled, “your bravery just needs a different spotlight.”

He held out a blank piece of paper. “We have our Bravery Chart here,” Pipkin offered. “But this village could also use charts for Kindness, for Listening, for Thoughtfulness! Mr. Higgins,” he continued, his voice full of energy, “with your unique knowledge of the deep and the quiet, and your excellent nose for what’s important, would you join me on an expedition to design them?”

Bartholomew blinked. He’d never been asked for his opinion before. He looked at Pipkin, Kit and Della, and Professor Pine, who nodded. He took a deep breath. Slowly, Bartholomew Higgins’ lips curved upwards. It wasn’t a wide grin, but a small, wobbly thing, like a new sprout pushing through hard ground. But it *was* a smile.

The villagers, who had gathered, gasped. Then, cheers rippled through the crowd. Pipkin beamed. He reached into his pocket, not for a sticker, but for a tiny golden crayon. With careful strokes, he drew a small, determined sprout beside Bartholomew’s name. It wasn't an ending. It was a brave, hopeful Willowbrook beginning.
